source_signature.text:
theorem exists_surjective_selectedAtomicCyclicIsometry
    (family : RepresentativeShellFamily)
    (L : MathlibAnnex.CStarAlgebra.PureState.GNSClass Limit →
      MathlibAnnex.CStarAlgebra.PureState.SelectedAtomicHilbert completedRootPureState →L[ℂ]
        MathlibAnnex.CStarAlgebra.PureState.SelectedAtomicHilbert completedRootPureState)
    (hLunit : ∀ i, L i ∈ unitary
      (MathlibAnnex.CStarAlgebra.PureState.SelectedAtomicHilbert completedRootPureState →L[ℂ]
        MathlibAnnex.CStarAlgebra.PureState.SelectedAtomicHilbert completedRootPureState))
    (hLsource : ∀ i n, (L i).comp (selectedAtomicRepresentation
      (transportedFlag family i n - transportedFlag family i (n + 1))) =
        representedShellLink family i n)
    (hLroot : L completedRootPureState.classOf = 1)
    {K : Type v} [NormedAddCommGroup K] [InnerProductSpace ℂ K]
    [CompleteSpace K] (rho : Representation (AtomicTarget L) K)
    (hrho : rho.IsIrreducible) :
    ∃ (eta_o : K) (eta : MathlibAnnex.CStarAlgebra.PureState.GNSClass Limit → K)
      (W : MathlibAnnex.CStarAlgebra.PureState.SelectedAtomicHilbert completedRootPureState →ₗᵢ[ℂ] K),
      Function.Surjective W ∧
      ‖eta_o‖ = 1 ∧
      (∀ i, ‖eta i‖ = 1) ∧
      (∀ i, W (MathlibAnnex.CStarAlgebra.PureState.selectedEmbedding completedRootPureState i
        (MathlibAnnex.CStarAlgebra.PureState.selectedVector completedRootPureState i)) = eta i) ∧
      (∀ i, (Unitary.linearIsometryEquiv
        (representedGeneratorUnitary L hLunit rho i) : K ≃ₗᵢ[ℂ] K)
          (eta i) = eta_o) ∧
      ∀ a,
        W.toContinuousLinearMap.comp (selectedAtomicRepresentation a) =
          ((restrictedRepresentation L rho) a).comp
            W.toContinuousLinearMap

content.assumptions:
Let $A$ be the completed CAR algebra, the completion of the matrix stages $M_{2^n}(\mathbb C)$ under $a\mapsto a\otimes I_2$. Let $f_n$ be the image of the first diagonal matrix unit, so $f_0=1$ and $f_n$ decreases through projections. The root state $\omega$ takes the value $a_{00}$ on each matrix stage.

Choose one pure state $\varphi_j$ from each unitary-equivalence class $j\in I$ of pure-state Gelfand-Naimark-Segal (GNS) representations, with root index $o$ and $\varphi_o=\omega$. Write $(H_j,\pi_j,\xi_j)$ for its complete complex GNS space, unital star representation and unit cyclic vector. Set $\mathcal H=\bigoplus_{j\in I}H_j$, $\pi=\bigoplus_j\pi_j$, and let $e_j:H_j\to \mathcal H$ be the coordinate embedding. No countability of $I$ is assumed. Inner products are linear in the second argument.

A supplied shell family consists of unital complex star automorphisms $\alpha_j$ and elements $w_{j,n}\in A$. Put $f_{j,n}=\alpha_j(f_n)$. The identities are $\varphi_j\circ\alpha_j=\omega$, $w_{j,n}^*w_{j,n}=f_{j,n}-f_{j,n+1}$ and $w_{j,n}w_{j,n}^*=f_n-f_{n+1}$. At the root, $\alpha_o$ is the identity and $w_{o,n}=f_n-f_{n+1}$. The family is an input, not an existence conclusion.

Let $L_j$ be unitaries on $\mathcal H$ satisfying $L_j\pi(f_{j,n}-f_{j,n+1})=\pi(w_{j,n})$ for all $j,n$, and assume $L_o=I_{\mathcal H}$. Let $T=C^*(\pi(A),\{L_j\})\subseteq B(\mathcal H)$ be the norm-closed unital star algebra they generate. Write $\iota(a)=\pi(a)$ as an element of $T$, and $g_j\in T$ for the element represented by $L_j$. Let $\rho:T\to B(K)$ be a unital complex star representation on a complete complex Hilbert space, put $\sigma=\rho\circ\iota$, and put $V_j=\rho(g_j)$. Assume $\rho$ is nonzero and irreducible: its only closed reducing subspaces are $\{0\}$ and $K$. This theorem does not assume the additional identity $L_j(e_j\xi_j)=e_o\xi_o$. The root normalization $L_o=I_{\mathcal H}$ is required.
content.conclusion: The selected cyclic pieces exhaust the target Hilbert space. [The source-restriction equivalence](https://github.com/r-tanaka-math/mathlib-annex/blob/437e6e46228bbb8e91211ebded349d7a30020e73/MathlibAnnex/Analysis/CStarAlgebra/CAR/CaptureRange.lean#L266-L293) is the direct consequence obtained by viewing the surjective isometry as a unitary. The representation being assumed irreducible is $\rho$ on $T$, not its generally reducible restriction $\sigma$ on $A$.
content.display_title: The cyclic sum fills every irreducible target representation
content.lean_realization_notes: The conclusion displayed here intertwines the CAR source. To obtain intertwining for every element of $T$, [the full capture theorem](https://github.com/r-tanaka-math/mathlib-annex/blob/437e6e46228bbb8e91211ebded349d7a30020e73/MathlibAnnex/Analysis/CStarAlgebra/CAR/Capture.lean#L28-L310) also uses the prescribed action $L_j(e_j\xi_j)=e_o\xi_o$. No multiplicity assertion for arbitrary reducible target representations and no unconditional existence of a shell family is claimed.
content.natural_language_statement:
Under the shell-family, generator and irreducibility assumptions below, there exist unit vectors $\zeta\in K$, $\eta_j\in K$ for $j\in I$, and a surjective complex-linear isometry $W:\mathcal H\to K$ such that

$W(e_j\xi_j)=\eta_j,\qquad V_j\eta_j=\zeta$

for every $j$, and $W\pi(a)=\sigma(a)W$ for every $a\in A$. In particular, $\sigma=\rho\circ\iota$ is unitarily equivalent to the selected atomic source representation $\pi$.
content.one_sentence_role: Uses shell reconstruction and residual lines to turn an isometric CAR intertwiner into a unitary equivalence on the source.

proof_steps.text: The common-root construction gives $\zeta$ and $\eta_j$ of norm one with the selected CAR vector states, $V_j\eta_j=\zeta$, and fixedness under their respective flags. Assemble the cyclic pieces into $W$. Its range $M$ is closed because $\mathcal H$ is complete and $W$ is an isometry. The relations for $a$ and $a^*$ show that $M$ reduces $\sigma$. Let $P_j$ project onto the common range of $\sigma(f_{j,n})$ and let $Q$ project onto the common range of $\sigma(f_n)$. Assembly gives $P_jM\subseteq\mathbb C\eta_j$.

Since $L_o=I_{\mathcal H}$, the represented root generator is $V_o=I_K$. Thus the root-index member $\eta_o$ equals the common vector $\zeta$. Consequently $\zeta\in M$ and $QM\subseteq\mathbb C\zeta$. Reconstruct $V_j=S_j+R_j$ with $R_j=V_jP_j$, $R_j^*R_j=P_j$, $R_jR_j^*=Q$ and $R_j=QR_jP_j$. The operators $S_j$ and $S_j^*$ are strong limits of finite sums of $\sigma(w_{j,n})$ and their adjoints. Closedness and source reduction make $M$ invariant under both limits.

Fixedness and the vector transport give $R_j\eta_j=\zeta$ and $R_j^*\zeta=\eta_j$. For $y\in M$, the vector $P_jy$ lies in $\mathbb C\eta_j$, so $R_jy\in\mathbb C\zeta\subseteq M$. For the adjoint, use $R_j^*=P_jR_j^*Q$ and $Qy\in\mathbb C\zeta$ to obtain $R_j^*y\in\mathbb C\eta_j\subseteq M$. Thus $M$ reduces the residual corner and, together with the shell sum, every $V_j$.

The orthogonal projection onto $M$ commutes with the represented source and every added generator. The commutation relation is stable under star-algebra operations and operator-norm limits, so $M$ reduces all of $\rho(T)$. It contains the unit vector $\zeta$ and is therefore nonzero. Irreducibility gives $M=K$, which is exactly surjectivity of $W$. Its pointed-vector and source intertwining identities are retained.

content.proof_summary: [The common-root vector-state theorem](https://github.com/r-tanaka-math/mathlib-annex/blob/437e6e46228bbb8e91211ebded349d7a30020e73/MathlibAnnex/Analysis/CStarAlgebra/CAR/CaptureSurviving.lean#L176-L250) supplies compatible unit vectors. [Cyclic-sum assembly](https://github.com/r-tanaka-math/mathlib-annex/blob/437e6e46228bbb8e91211ebded349d7a30020e73/MathlibAnnex/Analysis/CStarAlgebra/CAR/CyclicCapture.lean#L307-L461) gives an isometry with closed source-reducing range $M$. [Shell reconstruction](https://github.com/r-tanaka-math/mathlib-annex/blob/437e6e46228bbb8e91211ebded349d7a30020e73/MathlibAnnex/Analysis/CStarAlgebra/CAR/TargetReconstruction.lean#L121-L178) splits each represented generator into a strong shell sum and a residual corner. Both parts and their adjoints preserve $M$. [Norm-closed generation](https://github.com/r-tanaka-math/mathlib-annex/blob/437e6e46228bbb8e91211ebded349d7a30020e73/MathlibAnnex/Analysis/CStarAlgebra/AtomicConstruction/GeneratedReduction.lean#L36-L125) then makes $M$ a nonzero reducing subspace for $\rho$, so irreducibility forces $M=K$.

guide: Here `Limit` is $A$, `completedRootPureState` is the root state $\omega$ bundled with its purity proof, and `SelectedAtomicHilbert ...` is $\mathcal H$. `AtomicTarget L` is $T$ and `restrictedRepresentation L rho` is $\sigma$. Source `eta_o` denotes the common vector $\zeta$; `eta i` denotes $\eta_j$ at source index `i`. The equality of `eta` at the root index with `eta_o` follows from `hLroot`, rather than from their names. `Function.Surjective W` supplies the extra property that the isometry fills $K$. `hLsource` records the shell action; no hypothesis named `hLmap` occurs in this declaration.
